architectural_implications.before: Safety rules lived as instructions in the model's system prompt or context, enforced at the model's discretion.
architectural_implications.consequence: Policy becomes non-negotiable and testable independently of model behavior, but requires maintaining interception logic and anticipating which actions to block.
architectural_implications.observation: Governance constraints are implemented as deterministic hooks rather than as prompt instructions.

architectural_implications.after: Each stage reads a prior stage's artifact, forming an explicit, diffable handoff chain.
architectural_implications.before: Requirements and plans lived in chat history or tribal knowledge, and were re-explained per session.
architectural_implications.consequence: Context becomes reviewable and reproducible, and stage boundaries become contract boundaries between agents/humans.
architectural_implications.observation: Agent grounding context is externalized into chained version-controlled files (intent.md, spec.md, plan.md, REVIEW.md) rather than accumulated in conversation state.

architectural_implications.after: A fixed 20-50 task suite runs in GitHub Actions as a stage gate before accepting change.
architectural_implications.before: Model swaps or prompt/rule changes were validated manually or not at all.

architectural_implications.observation: Model and rule changes are gated by a real-task eval suite in CI.

core_insights.insight: The development lifecycle is driven by an ordered chain of versioned Markdown artifacts (intent.md → spec.md → plan.md) where each file has a distinct semantic role: intent.md = why, spec.md = what/expected behavior, plan.md = decomposed actionable tasks. This makes agent context an auditable repository artifact rather than ephemeral prompt text.

core_insights.insight: Self-verification is treated as a hard gate: the agent must have a machine-checkable way to verify its own work (tests, builds, lints, screenshot diffs) and pass test/lint/build with zero failures before it is allowed to report completion to a human.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Defining 'done' as passing an automated check rather than the agent's own assertion converts self-reported completion into an objectively falsifiable signal and reduces human review load.

core_insights.why_it_matters: It treats a model version change like a dependency upgrade, requiring regression evidence before accepting it, which is the operational mechanism for catching silent behavioral drift.

core_insights.why_it_matters: It separates governance (enforced by the runtime, not by instructions the model may ignore) from the model's reasoning, giving a hard boundary that cannot be talked around by prompt content.

deep_dives.trigger_insight: Always give Claude a way to verify its own work (tests, builds, lints, screenshot diffs) before an engineer sees it.

summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Eric
  • Channel: Eric Tech
  • Main topic: AI-Native Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) using Claude Code and Anthropic Playbook
  • Purpose: To guide viewers on how to apply the AI-Native SDLC Playbook in their own software development lifecycle using Claude Code, building apps with best practices and advanced agentic workflows. This video breaks down Anthropic's newly released 'AI-Native SDLC Playbook' for Claude Code, explaining how to transform every stage of software development—planning, designing, building, testing, deployment, and maintenance—using AI agents and modern development practices.

Topic Map

Introduction to AI-Native SDLC

  • Explanation: Explains what SDLC means and introduces Anthropic's AI-Native SDLC Playbook released by Boris Cherny and the Anthropic team.
  • Key claims:
    • Organizations write code at unprecedented speed with AI, but processes around code haven't changed.
    • Traditional SDLC runs in slow human loops; AI-native SDLC operates in hours, not weeks, with humans directing and governing.
  • Examples:
    • Claude Academy courses containing 14 lessons on AI-native SDLC.
  • Terminology:
    • SDLC
    • AI-Native SDLC Playbook
    • Claude Code
  • Why it matters: Understanding the shift from traditional human-speed development to agent-speed development.

Planning Stage (Intent)

  • Explanation: How planning works in AI-native SDLC using intent files and interactive interviews rather than committees and manual requirements gathering.
  • Key claims:
    • AI can interview developers via skills like 'grill-me' to gather requirements.
    • Conversations and decisions are captured in an intent.md file which is human-readable and machine-actionable.
  • Examples:
    • Claims status self-service intent.md template.
  • Terminology:
    • intent.md
    • grill-me skill
    • artifact chain
  • Why it matters: Streamlining requirement gathering into structured, machine-readable intent documents.

Design Stage (Spec)

  • Explanation: Converting intent into technical specs (spec.md).
  • Key claims:
    • intent.md defines the 'why', while spec.md defines the 'what', technical requirements, and expected behavior.
  • Examples:
    • Using prompts to instruct Claude to read intent.md and produce a requirements and design spec.
  • Terminology:
    • spec.md
    • design spec
  • Why it matters: Translating high-level intent into rigorous technical specifications for AI agents.

Building Stage (Plan)

  • Explanation: Converting intent and specs into an actionable implementation plan (plan.md).
  • Key claims:
    • plan.md takes intent and spec and breaks them into actionable tasks for AI agents to follow step-by-step or in parallel.
  • Examples:
    • Writing plan.md files using skills like writing-plans or superpowers.
  • Terminology:
    • plan.md
    • implementation plan
  • Why it matters: Structuring complex development tasks into manageable agent instructions.

Testing Stage & Feedback Loop

  • Explanation: Test-driven development (TDD), self-verification, and giving Claude feedback loops.
  • Key claims:
    • Always give Claude a way to verify its own work (tests, builds, lints, screenshot diffs) before an engineer sees it.
    • Verifying your work requires passing test, lint, and build checks.
  • Examples:
    • make test, make lint, make build commands ensuring zero failures before reporting done.
  • Terminology:
    • TDD
    • feedback loop
    • verifier subagent
  • Why it matters: Ensuring AI agents catch and fix their own errors before human review.

Continuous Evals in CI

  • Explanation: Running evaluation suites in CI to test agent performance after model swaps or rule changes.
  • Key claims:
    • Evals are the AI-native equivalent of stage-gate QA.
    • Collect 20 to 50 real tasks and run them as an eval suite in GitHub Actions.
  • Examples:
    • agent-evals.yml GitHub workflow configuration.
  • Terminology:
    • evals
    • CI/CD
    • regression test
  • Why it matters: Preventing model regressions and ensuring consistent agent output quality.

AI in PR Review Loop & Approval Gates

  • Explanation: How AI reviews pull requests and how hooks act as approval gates before production.
  • Key claims:
    • Claude reviews incoming PRs against organization policies and runs three passes (bugs, security, compliance).
    • Hooks act as guardrails to block unauthorized actions like editing certain files or touching production credentials.
  • Examples:
    • REVIEW.md file defining review instructions and pass criteria.
  • Terminology:
    • REVIEW.md
    • hooks
    • approval gates
  • Why it matters: Maintaining strict governance and safety over autonomous AI code changes.

CI/CD Integration & Maintenance

  • Explanation: Integrating Claude into deployment pipelines and maintaining systems via metric-driven loops.
  • Key claims:
    • Before deployment, Claude reads build logs and submits PRs for fixes; after deployment, it calls status tools to check releases.
    • Maintenance involves monitoring metrics and looping back to intent.md when issues arise.
  • Examples:
    • bands.yaml monitoring CI test failure rates over 30 days.
  • Terminology:
    • deployment
    • rollback
    • metrics
  • Why it matters: Closing the loop between production metrics and continuous improvement.

Key Points

Shift from Human Speed to Agent Speed

  • Explanation: Traditional SDLC is bottlenecked by manual building and planning; AI agents compress execution time drastically.
  • Evidence: Diagrams comparing traditional linear lines vs. AI-native fast loops.
  • Practical implication: Developers must focus on intent definition, review, and governance rather than boilerplate writing.

The Artifact Chain

  • Explanation: Development progresses systematically from intent.md to spec.md to plan.md, creating a clear audit trail and context for agents.
  • Evidence: Flowcharts showing document handoffs between stages.
  • Practical implication: Eliminates ambiguity in prompt engineering by maintaining structured Markdown files.

Self-Verification and TDD

  • Explanation: Agents must write tests first and use automated lint, test, and build commands to verify their own code before human intervention.
  • Evidence: Claude configuration snippets requiring all three checks to pass before reporting done.
  • Practical implication: Reduces human review overhead and catches bugs earlier in the cycle.

Frameworks, Models & Processes

AI-Native SDLC Lifecycle Loop

  • How it works: A continuous loop through Plan, Design, Build, Test, Deploy, and Maintain driven by Claude agents.
  • Components:
    • Plan (intent.md)
    • Design (spec.md)
    • Build (plan.md)
    • Test (TDD / Evals)
    • Deploy (CI/CD + Hooks)
    • Maintain (Metrics / bands.yaml)
  • When to use: When building applications using Claude Code and agentic workflows.

Examples & Case Studies

Creating a claims status self-service app intent document

  • Illustrates: How to capture user problems, proposed outcomes, affected users, and constraints in intent.md
  • Lesson: Structured markdown files provide clear intent for AI agents.

Setting up GitHub Actions eval workflows

  • Illustrates: Automating agent regression testing after model swaps
  • Lesson: Continuous evals ensure that updates to prompts or models do not break existing agent capabilities.

Actionable Takeaways

  • Immediate:
    • Adopt intent.md and spec.md patterns for project planning.
    • Implement self-verification checks (test, lint, build) for AI coding sessions.
    • Use hooks as approval gates to protect production environments.
  • Strategic:
    • Transition from human-speed coding to agent-speed SDLC governance.
    • Establish continuous evaluation pipelines for AI agent skills.
  • Questions to investigate:
    • How to integrate custom enterprise security policies into Claude Code hooks?
    • What is the optimal size for an eval test suite in CI?

Claims Worth Verifying

  • Claude Code and Anthropic team released the AI-Native SDLC Playbook (factual)
  • Evals using 20 to 50 real tasks can effectively catch regression when swapping AI models (best practice)

Notable Quotes

"Organizations have started using AI to write code at a speed unthinkable one year ago, yet the processes around the code haven't changed at the same pace." (at 0:07) "Always give Claude a way to verify its own work, whether tests, a build, or a screenshot diff." (at 15:21)

Compressed Summary

  • AI-native SDLC transforms traditional slow development loops into fast agentic loops.
  • Development follows an artifact chain from intent.md to spec.md to plan.md.
  • Agents must self-verify via test, lint, and build checks before reporting task completion.
  • Continuous evals in CI and hooks as approval gates ensure safety and prevent regression.
  • Keywords: sdlc, claude, agents, testing, ci
  • Core insight: AI-native software development replaces manual human bottlenecks with structured markdown intent files, self-verifying agent loops, and automated continuous evaluations.

  - intent.md defines the 'why', while spec.md defines the 'what', technical requirements, and expected behavior.
- **Examples**:
  - Using prompts to instruct Claude to read intent.md and produce a requirements and design spec.
- **Terminology**:
  - spec.md
  - design spec
- **Why it matters**: Translating high-level intent into rigorous technical specifications for AI agents.
### Building Stage (Plan)
- **Explanation**: Converting intent and specs into an actionable implementation plan (`plan.md`).
- **Key claims**:
  - plan.md takes intent and spec and breaks them into actionable tasks for AI agents to follow step-by-step or in parallel.
- **Examples**:
  - Writing plan.md files using skills like writing-plans or superpowers.
- **Terminology**:
  - plan.md
  - implementation plan
- **Why it matters**: Structuring complex development tasks into manageable agent instructions.
### Testing Stage & Feedback Loop
- **Explanation**: Test-driven development (TDD), self-verification, and giving Claude feedback loops.
- **Key claims**:
  - Always give Claude a way to verify its own work (tests, builds, lints, screenshot diffs) before an engineer sees it.
  - Verifying your work requires passing test, lint, and build checks.
- **Examples**:
  - make test, make lint, make build commands ensuring zero failures before reporting done.
- **Terminology**:
  - TDD
  - feedback loop
  - verifier subagent
- **Why it matters**: Ensuring AI agents catch and fix their own errors before human review.
### Continuous Evals in CI
- **Explanation**: Running evaluation suites in CI to test agent performance after model swaps or rule changes.
- **Key claims**:
  - Evals are the AI-native equivalent of stage-gate QA.
  - Collect 20 to 50 real tasks and run them as an eval suite in GitHub Actions.
- **Examples**:
  - agent-evals.yml GitHub workflow configuration.
- **Terminology**:
  - evals
  - CI/CD
  - regression test
- **Why it matters**: Preventing model regressions and ensuring consistent agent output quality.
### AI in PR Review Loop & Approval Gates
- **Explanation**: How AI reviews pull requests and how hooks act as approval gates before production.
- **Key claims**:
  - Claude reviews incoming PRs against organization policies and runs three passes (bugs, security, compliance).
  - Hooks act as guardrails to block unauthorized actions like editing certain files or touching production credentials.
- **Examples**:
  - REVIEW.md file defining review instructions and pass criteria.
- **Terminology**:
  - REVIEW.md
  - hooks
  - approval gates
- **Why it matters**: Maintaining strict governance and safety over autonomous AI code changes.
### CI/CD Integration & Maintenance
- **Explanation**: Integrating Claude into deployment pipelines and maintaining systems via metric-driven loops.
- **Key claims**:
  - Before deployment, Claude reads build logs and submits PRs for fixes; after deployment, it calls status tools to check releases.
  - Maintenance involves monitoring metrics and looping back to intent.md when issues arise.
- **Examples**:
  - bands.yaml monitoring CI test failure rates over 30 days.
- **Terminology**:
  - deployment
  - rollback
  - metrics
- **Why it matters**: Closing the loop between production metrics and continuous improvement.
## Key Points
### Shift from Human Speed to Agent Speed
- **Explanation**: Traditional SDLC is bottlenecked by manual building and planning; AI agents compress execution time drastically.
- **Evidence**: Diagrams comparing traditional linear lines vs. AI-native fast loops.
- **Practical implication**: Developers must focus on intent definition, review, and governance rather than boilerplate writing.
### The Artifact Chain
- **Explanation**: Development progresses systematically from intent.md to spec.md to plan.md, creating a clear audit trail and context for agents.
- **Evidence**: Flowcharts showing document handoffs between stages.
- **Practical implication**: Eliminates ambiguity in prompt engineering by maintaining structured Markdown files.
### Self-Verification and TDD
- **Explanation**: Agents must write tests first and use automated lint, test, and build commands to verify their own code before human intervention.
- **Evidence**: Claude configuration snippets requiring all three checks to pass before reporting done.
- **Practical implication**: Reduces human review overhead and catches bugs earlier in the cycle.
## Frameworks, Models & Processes
### AI-Native SDLC Lifecycle Loop
- **How it works**: A continuous loop through Plan, Design, Build, Test, Deploy, and Maintain driven by Claude agents.
- **Components**:
  - Plan (intent.md)
  - Design (spec.md)
  - Build (plan.md)
  - Test (TDD / Evals)
  - Deploy (CI/CD + Hooks)
  - Maintain (Metrics / bands.yaml)
- **When to use**: When building applications using Claude Code and agentic workflows.
## Examples & Case Studies
### Creating a claims status self-service app intent document
- **Illustrates**: How to capture user problems, proposed outcomes, affected users, and constraints in intent.md
- **Lesson**: Structured markdown files provide clear intent for AI agents.
### Setting up GitHub Actions eval workflows
- **Illustrates**: Automating agent regression testing after model swaps
- **Lesson**: Continuous evals ensure that updates to prompts or models do not break existing agent capabilities.
## Actionable Takeaways
- **Immediate**:
  - Adopt intent.md and spec.md patterns for project planning.
  - Implement self-verification checks (test, lint, build) for AI coding sessions.
  - Use hooks as approval gates to protect production environments.
- **Strategic**:
  - Transition from human-speed coding to agent-speed SDLC governance.
  - Establish continuous evaluation pipelines for AI agent skills.
- **Questions to investigate**:
  - How to integrate custom enterprise security policies into Claude Code hooks?
  - What is the optimal size for an eval test suite in CI?
## Claims Worth Verifying
- Claude Code and Anthropic team released the AI-Native SDLC Playbook (factual)
- Evals using 20 to 50 real tasks can effectively catch regression when swapping AI models (best practice)
## Notable Quotes
> "Organizations have started using AI to write code at a speed unthinkable one year ago, yet the processes around the code haven't changed at the same pace." (at 0:07)
> "Always give Claude a way to verify its own work, whether tests, a build, or a screenshot diff." (at 15:21)
## Compressed Summary
- AI-native SDLC transforms traditional slow development loops into fast agentic loops.
- Development follows an artifact chain from intent.md to spec.md to plan.md.
- Agents must self-verify via test, lint, and build checks before reporting task completion.
- Continuous evals in CI and hooks as approval gates ensure safety and prevent regression.
- **Keywords**: sdlc, claude, agents, testing, ci
- **Core insight**: AI-native software development replaces manual human bottlenecks with structured markdown intent files, self-verifying agent loops, and automated continuous evaluations.
